surface: SUNNYVAiLE LIBRAiRY / tool and application selection guide representative sample

readerContract.humanQuestion: Should I use ChatGPT, Claude or another tool for this job, and is paying actually worth it?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: The reader can choose the simplest adequate route from output, inputs, permissions, editability, rights, budget and verification needs rather than popularity or brand loyalty.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No technical background, paid plan or existing tool stack is assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: Tool choice is a constrained job match: desired final artifact plus allowed inputs, required actions, rights, cost and observable checks.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: The worked verdict compares a real Free Chat route with a paid file-working route for the same fictional workshop pack.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A task-led selection reference spanning writing, research, files, code, design, music, narration and other applications; vendor setup remains in the vendor books.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can say why this tool is adequate, what it cannot do, and what evidence would justify switching or paying.

canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Any change to the guide job, vendor-book boundary or task categories.
Before drafting and whenever product access, export, rights or pricing changes.
If any preserved run, setup record or comparison finding changes.
Any change to reference-book teaching requirements.
Any change to LAiDIES public prose rules.

strengthsToUse: Separate solid evidence, conditions and unknowns.
Give a useful action and recheck trigger.
patternsNotToCopy: Do not repeat the FAQ scaffold for every category.
Do not inherit dated tool claims.
Do not turn the guide into affiliate-style best-of lists.

glossaryAccumulation.producerGuard: Introduce product labels only after output and constraint decisions.
glossaryAccumulation.preventionEvidence: The sample begins with the workshop deliverable.

templateRepetition.producerGuard: Use a decision path and evidence table, not identical cards for every tool.
templateRepetition.preventionEvidence: The sample compares observed routes and ends with a conditional verdict.

referenceConfetti.producerGuard: Name tools only when they are genuine candidates for a specific job.
referenceConfetti.preventionEvidence: The sample includes only tested workshop routes and clearly labelled untested categories.

missingMechanism.producerGuard: Show how output, access, permissions, editability, rights, cost and checks determine the choice.
missingMechanism.preventionEvidence: Every verdict names the deciding constraint.

genericAction.producerGuard: Give a reusable decision card the reader can complete for one job.
genericAction.preventionEvidence: The reader records an adequate route and switch trigger.

jargonBeforeMeaning.producerGuard: Ask what must exist at the end before naming models or modes.
jargonBeforeMeaning.preventionEvidence: The opening starts with the deliverable.

disconnectedSystem.producerGuard: Connect generation, editing, export, permissions, rights and checking.
disconnectedSystem.preventionEvidence: The decision path continues through final usable artifact.

joylessInstruction.producerGuard: Use decisive candid verdicts rather than a generic matrix dump.
joylessInstruction.preventionEvidence: The paid-versus-Free result has a clear practical consequence.

purposeTooNarrow.producerGuard: The workshop is one worked selection case inside a broader task-category system.
purposeTooNarrow.preventionEvidence: Transfer routes cover media, research, files and code without pretending they were tested.

mechanismBeforeMotivation.producerGuard: Open with wasted subscriptions and unfinished outputs as the reader problem.
mechanismBeforeMotivation.preventionEvidence: The seven-factor method follows the practical stakes.

workedExampleOvertakesBookPurpose.producerGuard: Separate the tested verdict from broader untested routing cards.
workedExampleOvertakesBookPurpose.preventionEvidence: No workshop result is used to rank music, narration or design tools.

technicalExplainerVoice.producerGuard: Write as a decisive buyer's and maker's guide, not procurement software documentation.
technicalExplainerVoice.preventionEvidence: Each technical boundary is translated into time, money, risk or usable output.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Choose the simplest route that can legally and practically create the final editable artifact from allowed inputs, perform only authorized actions and expose checks you can run; pay only when a measured bottleneck remains.
causalSequence: Name the final usable artifact and non-negotiable constraints.
Remove tools that cannot access the allowed inputs or export the required format.
Compare the remaining routes on permissions, editability, rights, cost and verification.
Use the workshop runs to distinguish useful Free output from paid execution without claiming a universal winner.
Set a switch trigger so the reader knows what evidence would justify another product or plan.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: ChatGPT Free Chat versus paid Claude Code Sonnet 5 Medium/High for the same fictional workshop pack.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: Select a narration or music route by commercial rights, voice consent, editability, export and budget before comparing generation quality.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Complete one seven-factor decision card and write the exact condition that would make the current adequate route insufficient.

humourPlan.lessonJob: Use one restrained line about buying a subscription before identifying the bottleneck; avoid brand-team jokes.

draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Answer-first verdict, seven-factor chooser, observed comparison, switch triggers, untested-category boundaries and dated cards.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Use concise decision paths and a few deep worked cases; avoid a giant symmetrical catalogue of tools.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Make the hidden dependencies between an attractive generation, an editable export, lawful use and a checked final artifact visible.

humanQuestion.reason: Readers face brands before they have defined the job.
humanQuestion.plannedEvidence: Open with whether this workshop requires payment.

usefulCuriosity.reason: The paid route was not automatically more accurate.
usefulCuriosity.plannedEvidence: Ask what paid access changed before revealing the findings.

invisibleProcessConcrete.reason: Export, rights and permissions are hidden behind demos.
invisibleProcessConcrete.plannedEvidence: Show them as non-compensable decision factors.

familiarTechnicalMovement.reason: Model and tool distinctions matter only through the finished job.
familiarTechnicalMovement.plannedEvidence: Move from the workshop documents to execution environment and checks.

limitationsConsequences.reason: The tested products and untested categories must not blur.
limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: Keep every conclusion bound to plan, surface and date.

humourSurprise.reason: A light line can expose subscription-first thinking.
humourSurprise.plannedEvidence: Use it once before the switch-trigger method.

betterNextQuestion.reason: The reader needs a future-proof choice.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: End with what bottleneck would make you switch.

explanationArc.adaptation: The guide uses answer-first routing and one exact comparison rather than a lecture.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: The guide could become a popularity list, imply a paid winner from incomparable environments or make untested media-rights recommendations.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Draft the honest workshop verdict with observed limitations and a reusable seven-factor chooser; label every media route as research-only until tested.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A reader can justify an adequate Free or paid route and name the evidence that would change the decision without treating brand or subscription as quality proof.
